scr_ar_duplicating_a_customer_group.purpose: Creates a new customer group by copying an existing one — for example copying 'Retail Tenants' to build 'Retail Tenants — Phase 2' for a newly delivered retail podium.
scr_ar_duplicating_a_customer_group.outcome: A related grouping set up quickly with the same filters as its source.
scr_ar_duplicating_a_customer_group.rootCause: Many customer groups differ only slightly; copying preserves filter logic that already works and reduces the chance of building a group that silently excludes customers.
scr_ar_duplicating_a_customer_group.ifSkipped: Similar groups are rebuilt from scratch with inconsistent filters.
redFlags: Duplicated groups left with the source's name

scr_ar_printing_customer_group_details.purpose: Prints a customer group's definition and members for documentation, for example to show an owner exactly which tenants are included in the 'Affiliates' receivable line.
scr_ar_printing_customer_group_details.outcome: A documented record of how a reporting category is composed.
scr_ar_printing_customer_group_details.rootCause: When owners question a category total, a printed membership list shows exactly which customers were included and answers the question without system access.
scr_ar_printing_customer_group_details.ifSkipped: Category totals cannot be explained to owners without extra work.
redFlags: Printed membership differing from current membership

scr_ar_exporting_customer_group_details.purpose: Exports a customer group's definition and members to a file for review or reuse in another company.
scr_ar_exporting_customer_group_details.outcome: Group membership available for bulk review in a spreadsheet.
scr_ar_exporting_customer_group_details.rootCause: Reviewing large groups for misclassified customers is easier in a spreadsheet, particularly after acquisitions add many new tenants at once.
scr_ar_exporting_customer_group_details.ifSkipped: Misclassified customers in large groups go unnoticed.
redFlags: Exports not reconciled back after cleanup

scr_ar_customer_types_list.purpose: Lists customer types — classifications such as Commercial Tenant, Affiliate, Ancillary Vendor, Insurance Carrier — with actions to add, edit, duplicate, print and export.
scr_ar_customer_types_list.outcome: A consistent classification scheme for non-resident customers.
scr_ar_customer_types_list.rootCause: Customer type drives default accounts and reporting; a consistent list ensures, for example, that every affiliate posts to Due From Affiliates rather than trade receivables.
scr_ar_customer_types_list.ifSkipped: Similar customers are classified differently and post to different accounts.

scr_ar_adding_customer_types.purpose: Adds a customer type — for example 'Cell Tower Licensee' — with any defaults it should carry.
scr_ar_adding_customer_types.outcome: New customer categories available for classification.
scr_ar_adding_customer_types.rootCause: New revenue streams (EV charging operators, solar lease partners) need their own type so their receivables and revenue are reported separately.
scr_ar_adding_customer_types.ifSkipped: New revenue streams are lumped into generic categories.

scr_ar_customer_type_information_page.purpose: The customer type record page with its name, description and any default settings.
scr_ar_customer_type_information_page.outcome: A complete definition of the customer category.
scr_ar_customer_type_information_page.rootCause: Clear definitions let staff classify new customers consistently, which keeps category reporting reliable over time.

scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_customer_type.purpose: Edits or views a customer type's name, description and defaults — for example changing the 'Affiliate' type's default receivable to Due From Affiliates.
scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_customer_type.outcome: Customer type definitions stay aligned with reporting needs.
scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_customer_type.rootCause: Changing a type's defaults affects future invoices for every customer of that type, so edits must be deliberate and coordinated with accounting.
scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_customer_type.ifSkipped: Outdated type defaults keep sending revenue to wrong accounts.

scr_ar_deleting_customer_types.purpose: Deletes a customer type that no customer uses — for example a type created during setup testing — so staff cannot classify new customers into it.
scr_ar_deleting_customer_types.rootCause: Unused types clutter selection lists and invite misclassification of new customers; types in use are protected from deletion.
scr_ar_deleting_customer_types.ifSkipped: New customers are assigned obsolete types.

scr_ar_printing_customer_types.purpose: Prints the list of customer types and their definitions, creating a record for documentation or training.
scr_ar_printing_customer_types.outcome: A reference sheet of customer categories for staff.
scr_ar_printing_customer_types.rootCause: Offshore staff classifying new customers need a clear reference; printed definitions reduce inconsistent classification.
scr_ar_printing_customer_types.ifSkipped: Staff guess at categories and classification drifts.

scr_ar_duplicating_customer_types.purpose: Adds a customer type by copying an existing one and editing it — for example creating 'Office Tenant' from 'Retail Tenant' with the same defaults.
scr_ar_duplicating_customer_types.outcome: Related types created quickly with consistent settings.
scr_ar_duplicating_customer_types.rootCause: Copying keeps defaults consistent across related types, for example two kinds of commercial tenant.
scr_ar_duplicating_customer_types.ifSkipped: Related types are created with inconsistent defaults.

scr_ar_exporting_customer_types.purpose: Exports customer types to CSV or other formats for review or transfer to another company.
scr_ar_exporting_customer_types.outcome: Customer type setup available outside the system.
scr_ar_exporting_customer_types.rootCause: Standardizing customer types across companies (e.g., after a merger of management platforms) requires moving definitions between them.
scr_ar_exporting_customer_types.ifSkipped: Types are re-keyed manually across companies.
redFlags: Exported and re-imported types creating duplicates

scr_ar_customers_in_a_multi_entity_share.purpose: Explains how customers work in a multi-entity shared company — one customer list across many legal entities, with visibility restrictions controlling which entities can bill each customer.
scr_ar_customers_in_a_multi_entity_share.outcome: Users understand how to share or restrict customers across owners' entities.
scr_ar_customers_in_a_multi_entity_share.rootCause: Management companies run many owners' properties in one shared company. Without restrictions, any entity could invoice any customer, putting revenue in the wrong owner's books.
scr_ar_customers_in_a_multi_entity_share.ifSkipped: Revenue and receivables land in the wrong legal entity.

scr_ar_enabling_customer_restrictions.purpose: Enables customer visibility restrictions in the Multi Entity Console, which requires administrator-level access.
scr_ar_enabling_customer_restrictions.outcome: Customer visibility can be limited by entity.
scr_ar_enabling_customer_restrictions.rootCause: Restrictions are off by default; until enabled, every entity sees every customer, which is inappropriate for multi-owner management companies.
scr_ar_enabling_customer_restrictions.ifSkipped: Customers remain visible and billable by all entities.
redFlags: Restrictions never enabled in multi-owner companies

scr_ar_multi_entity_customer_restriction.purpose: Describes how customer restrictions limit invoicing and reporting of a customer to specific entities.
scr_ar_multi_entity_customer_restriction.outcome: Each customer is billed only by the entities it has contracts with.
scr_ar_multi_entity_customer_restriction.rootCause: A retail tenant has a lease with one property's entity; only that entity should invoice it and carry its receivable.
scr_ar_multi_entity_customer_restriction.ifSkipped: Tenants are invoiced by the wrong entity and revenue is misallocated between owners.
redFlags: Invoices to restricted customers from other entities

scr_ar_displaying_the_customer_visibilit.purpose: Opens the Customer Visibility list showing which entities can see each customer.
scr_ar_displaying_the_customer_visibilit.outcome: A reviewable map of customer-to-entity access.
scr_ar_displaying_the_customer_visibilit.rootCause: Periodic review of visibility catches customers that became visible too broadly after setup changes.
scr_ar_displaying_the_customer_visibilit.ifSkipped: Visibility drifts and cross-entity billing errors appear.

scr_ar_customer_visibility_list.purpose: Lists customers with their visibility restrictions by entity, where restrictions are viewed, edited and exported.
scr_ar_customer_visibility_list.outcome: Central control over which entities can bill each customer.
scr_ar_customer_visibility_list.rootCause: In portfolios with many owners, visibility is the primary control keeping one owner's tenants out of another owner's receivables.
scr_ar_customer_visibility_list.ifSkipped: Cross-owner billing errors occur and require intercompany corrections.

scr_ar_creating_the_list_view_that_inclu.purpose: Configures the Customer Visibility list view (columns and filters) before exporting it.
scr_ar_creating_the_list_view_that_inclu.outcome: Exports contain exactly the visibility data needed for review.
scr_ar_creating_the_list_view_that_inclu.rootCause: A tailored view keeps the export focused on the restriction fields that auditors and administrators review.
scr_ar_creating_the_list_view_that_inclu.ifSkipped: Exports are cluttered or miss key fields.

scr_ar_exporting_the_customer_restrictio.purpose: Exports the customer restrictions (visibility) list to a spreadsheet for an access review of which entities can bill which customers.
scr_ar_exporting_the_customer_restrictio.rootCause: Periodic access reviews of who can bill whom are easier in a spreadsheet, especially in large multi-owner companies.
scr_ar_exporting_the_customer_restrictio.ifSkipped: Periodic access reviews of customer visibility are not performed.

scr_ar_viewing_and_editing_a_customers_v.purpose: Views or changes which entities can see and bill a specific customer — for example restricting a tenant to the property entity named on its lease.
scr_ar_viewing_and_editing_a_customers_v.rootCause: Restrictions must mirror contracts; when a lease is assigned to a new entity after a sale or recapitalization, visibility must change too.
scr_ar_viewing_and_editing_a_customers_v.ifSkipped: The old entity keeps billing a customer it no longer has a contract with.
redFlags: Visibility not updated after property sales

scr_ar_required_fields_for_new_customer_.purpose: Lists the fields required when adding a new customer restriction (customer, entity, access type).
scr_ar_required_fields_for_new_customer_.outcome: Restrictions are created completely and correctly.
scr_ar_required_fields_for_new_customer_.rootCause: Incomplete restrictions may fail silently or apply too broadly; knowing the required fields avoids both.
scr_ar_required_fields_for_new_customer_.ifSkipped: Restrictions are incomplete and do not protect entity boundaries.

scr_ar_guidelines_for_updating_customer_.purpose: Guidelines for changing customer restrictions safely, including effects on open invoices and reporting.
scr_ar_guidelines_for_updating_customer_.outcome: Restriction changes do not strand open receivables.
scr_ar_guidelines_for_updating_customer_.rootCause: Restricting a customer away from an entity that still has open invoices can hide those receivables from that entity's users.
scr_ar_guidelines_for_updating_customer_.ifSkipped: Open receivables become invisible to the entity that must collect them.
redFlags: Restrictions changed while invoices are open

scr_ar_printing_customer_visibility_deta.purpose: Prints customer visibility details — which entities can see and bill each customer — as retained evidence for SOC or internal audit access reviews.
scr_ar_printing_customer_visibility_deta.outcome: Evidence of customer access controls for auditors.
scr_ar_printing_customer_visibility_deta.rootCause: SOC and internal audits test logical access controls, including which entities can transact with which customers.
scr_ar_printing_customer_visibility_deta.ifSkipped: Access control evidence is unavailable at audit.
redFlags: No retained evidence of access reviews

scr_ar_updating_multiple_customer_visibi.purpose: Updates visibility restrictions for many customers at once — typically after a portfolio sale or entity restructuring.
scr_ar_updating_multiple_customer_visibi.outcome: Bulk changes to customer access applied consistently.
scr_ar_updating_multiple_customer_visibi.rootCause: Portfolio transactions change entity relationships for many customers at once; bulk updates avoid missing some.
scr_ar_updating_multiple_customer_visibi.ifSkipped: Some customers keep outdated entity access after the transaction.

scr_ar_billing.purpose: Chapter on billing non-resident customers in A/R — sales invoices, recurring invoices, and bill-backs of utilities and shared expenses to tenants and affiliates.
scr_ar_billing.outcome: Non-resident revenue and cost recoveries are invoiced and tracked as receivables.
scr_ar_billing.rootCause: Commercial rent, CAM recoveries, ancillary contract revenue and affiliate bill-backs are contractual amounts owed to the property; unless invoiced through A/R, they are neither recognized nor collected.
scr_ar_billing.ifSkipped: Revenue and cost recoveries are missed or collected informally without records.
redFlags: Bill-backs not tying to underlying expenses

scr_ar_a_r_invoices_list_a_r_sales_invoi.purpose: Lists A/R sales invoices with customer, date, amount, state (draft, posted, partially paid, paid, reversed) and actions to add, view, edit, reverse or delete.
scr_ar_a_r_invoices_list_a_r_sales_invoi.outcome: A register of everything billed to non-resident customers and its status.
scr_ar_a_r_invoices_list_a_r_sales_invoi.rootCause: Tracking invoice state is how accountants know what is outstanding, what has been paid, and what needs follow-up before month-end.
scr_ar_a_r_invoices_list_a_r_sales_invoi.ifSkipped: Unpaid invoices are not followed up and drafts are never posted.
redFlags: Draft invoices older than the current period

scr_ar_managing_a_r_invoices.purpose: Explains managing A/R invoices — adding, editing, deleting, reversing — and how each action affects the GL.
scr_ar_managing_a_r_invoices.outcome: Invoices are corrected using the right method for their state.
scr_ar_managing_a_r_invoices.rootCause: Drafts can be edited or deleted freely, but posted invoices need reversal to preserve the audit trail; using the wrong method corrupts the ledger.
scr_ar_managing_a_r_invoices.ifSkipped: Posted invoices are altered incorrectly and the subledger breaks.

scr_ar_viewing_the_a_r_invoices_list.purpose: Views and filters the A/R invoices list, drilling into invoices from the top level.
scr_ar_viewing_the_a_r_invoices_list.outcome: Quick identification of invoices by customer, state or date.
scr_ar_viewing_the_a_r_invoices_list.rootCause: Month-end review of open and draft invoices begins with a filtered list; drafts left unposted mean revenue is missing, and open invoices past due need collection follow-up before the aging goes to the owner.
scr_ar_viewing_the_a_r_invoices_list.ifSkipped: Open or draft invoices are overlooked at close.

scr_ar_viewing_an_a_r_invoice.purpose: Opens an A/R invoice to see header, line items, GL distribution, payments applied and state.
scr_ar_viewing_an_a_r_invoice.rootCause: Customer disputes and audit samples require the invoice detail, including which accounts it credited and what has been paid.
scr_ar_viewing_an_a_r_invoice.ifSkipped: Disputes and audit requests take longer to answer.

scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_invoice_workflow.purpose: Describes the workflow for adding an A/R sales invoice: header, default line information, line items, then finish as draft or post.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_invoice_workflow.outcome: Invoices entered consistently with correct defaults.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_invoice_workflow.rootCause: Following the same workflow ensures each invoice carries the right customer, terms, accounts and dimensions.
scr_ar_adding_an_a_r_invoice_workflow.ifSkipped: Invoices are entered inconsistently and post to wrong accounts.

scr_ar_entering_basic_information_about_.purpose: Enters the invoice header — customer, invoice date, due date, terms, reference and description.
scr_ar_entering_basic_information_about_.outcome: A correctly dated and addressed invoice header.
scr_ar_entering_basic_information_about_.rootCause: Invoice date determines the revenue period and due date drives aging; errors here misstate both.
scr_ar_entering_basic_information_about_.ifSkipped: Revenue lands in the wrong period and aging is wrong.
redFlags: Invoice dates in prior closed periods

scr_ar_selecting_default_information_for.purpose: Sets default values (GL account, location, department) applied to all invoice lines.
scr_ar_selecting_default_information_for.rootCause: Defaults reduce keying and ensure all lines of an invoice (e.g., a CAM bill with several components) post to the same property and department.
scr_ar_selecting_default_information_for.ifSkipped: Lines are coded inconsistently within one invoice.
redFlags: Defaults set to the wrong location

scr_ar_entering_line_items_in_an_a_r_inv.purpose: Enters invoice lines — description, quantity, amount, revenue account, location and dimensions — for each item billed.
scr_ar_entering_line_items_in_an_a_r_inv.outcome: Each billed item is recorded to the correct revenue or recovery account.
scr_ar_entering_line_items_in_an_a_r_inv.rootCause: Different items on one invoice (base rent, CAM estimate, utility recovery) belong in different revenue accounts; line-level coding keeps revenue analysis accurate.
scr_ar_entering_line_items_in_an_a_r_inv.ifSkipped: Revenue categories such as base rent, CAM and utility recovery are misstated.
redFlags: All lines coded to one revenue account

scr_ar_finish_the_invoice.purpose: Completes the invoice — adding rows, attachments and choosing to save as draft or post.
scr_ar_finish_the_invoice.outcome: The invoice is either held for review or posted to the GL.
scr_ar_finish_the_invoice.rootCause: Posting recognizes revenue and the receivable; review before posting catches errors while they are still easy to fix.
scr_ar_finish_the_invoice.ifSkipped: Invoices stay in draft and revenue is missing, or errors are posted without review.

scr_ar_saving_a_transaction_as_a_draft.purpose: Saves an A/R invoice as a draft — with no GL effect until posted — so a large or unusual billing such as an annual CAM reconciliation can be reviewed first.
scr_ar_saving_a_transaction_as_a_draft.outcome: Invoices can be prepared and reviewed before affecting the books.
scr_ar_saving_a_transaction_as_a_draft.rootCause: Draft status allows a reviewer to check large or unusual invoices (e.g., annual CAM reconciliations) before revenue is recognized.
scr_ar_saving_a_transaction_as_a_draft.ifSkipped: Unreviewed invoices post directly, or drafts are forgotten and never posted.

scr_ar_editing_an_a_r_invoice.purpose: Edits an A/R invoice — freely while draft; for posted invoices, only fields allowed without reversal.
scr_ar_editing_an_a_r_invoice.outcome: Invoice corrections made through the appropriate path.
scr_ar_editing_an_a_r_invoice.rootCause: Posted invoices affect the GL and customer ledgers; restricting edits preserves the audit trail.
scr_ar_editing_an_a_r_invoice.ifSkipped: Errors persist, or posted invoices are altered in ways that break reconciliations.

scr_ar_importing_a_r_invoices.purpose: Imports A/R invoices in bulk from a template — for example monthly utility bill-backs to many commercial tenants or opening balances at onboarding.
scr_ar_importing_a_r_invoices.outcome: Large billing runs created accurately in one step.
scr_ar_importing_a_r_invoices.rootCause: Bill-backs and onboarding balances involve many invoices; importing avoids keying errors and missed customers.
scr_ar_importing_a_r_invoices.ifSkipped: Bill-backs are keyed manually and some are missed.
redFlags: Import totals not tied to source expense

scr_ar_deleting_or_reversing_invoices.purpose: Explains when to delete an invoice (drafts) versus reverse it (posted), preserving the audit trail.
scr_ar_deleting_or_reversing_invoices.outcome: Incorrect invoices removed through the proper method.
scr_ar_deleting_or_reversing_invoices.rootCause: Deleting posted invoices would remove revenue and receivables with no trace; reversal records the correction.
scr_ar_deleting_or_reversing_invoices.ifSkipped: Posted invoices vanish without trace, or wrong invoices remain.
redFlags: Frequent reversals for the same customer

scr_ar_viewing_an_invoices_state.purpose: Shows an invoice's state — draft, posted, partially paid, paid, reversed — from the invoices list.
scr_ar_viewing_an_invoices_state.outcome: Clarity on which correction path applies and whether follow-up is needed.
scr_ar_viewing_an_invoices_state.rootCause: The allowed actions depend on state; knowing it prevents attempts to edit paid invoices or chase paid balances.
scr_ar_viewing_an_invoices_state.ifSkipped: Wrong corrections are attempted and paid customers are chased.
redFlags: Partially paid invoices with no follow-up

scr_ar_configuring_invoices_for_reversal.purpose: Configures A/R so posted invoices can be reversed, including unpaid invoice reversal settings.
scr_ar_configuring_invoices_for_reversal.outcome: Posted invoice errors can be corrected with an audit trail.
scr_ar_configuring_invoices_for_reversal.rootCause: Without reversal enabled, accountants resort to manual credit adjustments that obscure what was corrected.
scr_ar_configuring_invoices_for_reversal.ifSkipped: Corrections are made by ad hoc adjustments that are hard to audit.
redFlags: Reversal disabled while errors are corrected by adjustments

scr_ar_clearing_a_negative_invoice.purpose: Clears a negative invoice (a credit) by applying it against positive invoices or refunding it.
scr_ar_clearing_a_negative_invoice.outcome: Customer credits are used or refunded rather than left open.
scr_ar_clearing_a_negative_invoice.rootCause: Negative invoices represent money owed back to the customer; left open, they distort aging and may become unclaimed property.
scr_ar_clearing_a_negative_invoice.ifSkipped: Credits linger, aging is misstated and escheat exposure grows.

scr_ar_reversing_an_invoice.purpose: Reverses a posted invoice, creating offsetting entries so revenue and the receivable are removed with an audit trail.
scr_ar_reversing_an_invoice.outcome: An incorrect invoice is cancelled cleanly.
scr_ar_reversing_an_invoice.rootCause: Invoices billed to the wrong customer or amount must be removed without destroying history; reversal does that.
scr_ar_reversing_an_invoice.ifSkipped: Wrong invoices remain in revenue and receivables.

scr_ar_enabling_invoice_reversal.purpose: Turns on invoice reversal in A/R configuration (Enable Functionality) so posted invoices billed in error can be reversed with an audit trail instead of manual adjustments.
scr_ar_enabling_invoice_reversal.rootCause: The reversal function must be switched on before posted invoice errors can be corrected with a trail.
scr_ar_enabling_invoice_reversal.ifSkipped: Errors are corrected with manual adjustments instead.

scr_ar_reversing_a_paid_invoice.purpose: Reverses an invoice that is partially paid or paid, which requires first dealing with the associated payment (reversing or reapplying it).
scr_ar_reversing_a_paid_invoice.outcome: Paid invoices billed in error are corrected along with their payments.
scr_ar_reversing_a_paid_invoice.rootCause: A paid invoice has a payment attached; reversing the invoice alone would leave an unapplied payment and a misstated ledger.
scr_ar_reversing_a_paid_invoice.ifSkipped: Payments become orphaned and customer balances are wrong.

scr_ar_reversing_an_unpaid_a_r_invoice.purpose: Reverses an unpaid posted A/R invoice from Search & Find, removing it from revenue and receivables.
scr_ar_reversing_an_unpaid_a_r_invoice.rootCause: Unpaid invoices raised in error overstate revenue and receivables and lead to collection calls on amounts not owed.
scr_ar_reversing_an_unpaid_a_r_invoice.ifSkipped: Customers are chased for invalid charges and revenue is overstated.

scr_ar_deleting_an_a_r_invoice.purpose: Deletes an A/R invoice record — only appropriate for drafts or invoices entered in error before any activity.
scr_ar_deleting_an_a_r_invoice.rootCause: Deleting is safe only when the invoice never affected the GL; otherwise reversal is required to keep the trail.
scr_ar_deleting_an_a_r_invoice.ifSkipped: Duplicate draft invoices are posted by mistake.
